items.title: Verstappen tops final practice; top five fit inside 0.274s
items.summary: The official 22-car FP3 classification has Max Verstappen first in 1:11.622, 0.025s ahead of Kimi Antonelli; Lando Norris is third at +0.131s, George Russell fourth at +0.184s and Charles Leclerc fifth at +0.274s. Formula1.com's report says Hamilton's session ended early after vibration and smoke reports, and rain arrived at the finish. FIA Document 32's classification matches the Formula1.com result table.
items.why_it_matters: The top five are tightly grouped, but this is a single practice session rather than a qualifying order. Verstappen's 30-place penalty and the decision's conditional grid allocation make the official starting order important.

items.title: Verstappen receives 30-place drop after power-unit changes
items.summary: Formula1.com reports 10-place drops for Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after Ferrari fitted fifth ICEs. The Stewards' Document 33 imposes a 30-place drop on Max Verstappen for his fifth ICE, turbocharger and exhaust. If Car 3 is classified in Qualifying, the decision assigns its Race grid position under Article B2.5.4.b.iv, superseding the earlier back-of-grid report. FIA Document 30 separately records parts for Sergio Perez but does not determine his exact grid position; George Russell's five-place penalty is a separate ruling.
items.why_it_matters: Component declarations and penalty decisions are distinct. The official qualifying classification and grid determine how the 30-place sanction is applied; do not infer Perez's place from the Technical Delegate's component table.

items.title: Perez summoned over an alleged unsafe condition after FP3
items.summary: FIA Document 31 summons Sergio Perez (Car 11) and a Cadillac representative over the alleged unsafe condition of Car 3 at 12:22 BRT. They were required to report to the Stewards at 13:00 BRT. The latest reviewed event listing at 15:55 UTC still showed the summons, not a decision.
items.why_it_matters: This is an allegation, not a finding or penalty. Recheck the FIA listing before saying how the matter was resolved.

items.title: Mercedes can clinch the constructors' title with a three-point gain
items.summary: The latest official standings show Mercedes on 630 points, 126 ahead of Ferrari on 504. Formula1.com's pre-weekend scenario says Mercedes clinches the constructors' title if it gains three points on Ferrari in Brazil; the practice sessions have not changed the standings.
items.why_it_matters: The Drivers' title is already settled, but the teams' championship remains live. Practice awards no points, so the three-point threshold is still a race-weekend scenario.

items.title: Sao Paulo Grand Prix contract extended through 2035
items.summary: Formula1.com reports a new five-year agreement that keeps the Sao Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos on the Formula 1 calendar through 2035.
items.why_it_matters: The extension gives the venue a long-term place on the calendar beyond the immediate championship weekend.
